bug_semantics: An authenticated caller can submit one /v1/completions request whose prompt is an arbitrarily long outer list of strings or token-id lists. The renderer preserves that outer cardinality; completion serving iterates every rendered input, creates one engine generator and request ID per element, merges all generators, and allocates response state proportional to the prompt count. Per-prompt token and sampling limits therefore do not bound aggregate CPU, memory, async-task, scheduler-slot, or response-buffer consumption for the HTTP request.
flaw_origin: PR #2529 intentionally enabled batch completions. Its first member commit d04fd49c2bc9540237d3d11b6d1de26bbc35d232 removed the explicit rejection of len(prompts) > 1 and replaced the single engine.generate call with an unbounded loop that appends one generator per prompt, merges them, and sizes streaming/non-streaming response arrays by the number of prompts. It added functional batch tests but no outer prompt-count or aggregate backend-request bound. The second member only added type hints; the main-branch landing 3a7dd7e367277c47472912e84375fa912df07328 squashed both members.
